## Claims
- [proved] For \(p_a(t)=[z^t]\prod_{k=1}^a(1-z^k)^{-1}\), with \(p_a(t)=0\) for \(t<0\),
\[
\#\{\rho\subseteq b^a:|\rho|=N\}
=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,a\}}(-1)^{|S|}
p_a\!\left(N-|S|b-\sum_{s\in S}s\right).
\]
- [proved] Complementation \(\rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1)\) gives
\[
\#\{\rho\subseteq b^a:|\rho|=N\}
=\#\{\rho\subseteq b^a:|\rho|=ab-N\}.
\]
- [proved] Conditional on the accepted graded integral basis \(Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho\), \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}Q_{ij+N}
=\sum_{S\subseteq[a]}(-1)^{|S|}
p_a\!\left(N-|S|b-\sum_{s\in S}s\right),
\]
and \(Q_{ij+N}\) is free abelian, vanishing unless \(0\le N\le ab\).

## Strategy
Let
\[
R_{a,b}(z)=\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}.
\]
Splitting partitions according as their first row is \(<b\) or equals \(b\) gives
\[
R_{a,b}=R_{a,b-1}+z^bR_{a-1,b},
\qquad R_{a,0}=R_{0,b}=1.
\]
The product
\[
\prod_{k=1}^a\frac{1-z^{b+k}}{1-z^k}
\]
satisfies this same recurrence and these boundary conditions. Hence
\[
R_{a,b}(z)=\prod_{k=1}^a\frac{1-z^{b+k}}{1-z^k}
=\left(\prod_{s=1}^a(1-z^{b+s})\right)
\left(\prod_{k=1}^a(1-z^k)^{-1}\right).
\]
Expanding the numerator,
\[
\prod_{s=1}^a(1-z^{b+s})
=\sum_{S\subseteq[a]}(-1)^{|S|}
z^{|S|b+\sum_{s\in S}s}.
\]
Taking \([z^N]\) proves the requested formula.

For padded \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\), \(\rho^\vee\) lies in \(b^a\), is involutive, and has
\[
|\rho^\vee|=\sum_{k=1}^a(b-\rho_k)=ab-|\rho|,
\]
proving complement symmetry. Under the stated basis hypothesis for \(Q\), counting basis elements of degree \(ij+N\) gives the displayed rank formula and freeness.

## Gaps
The conclusions about \(Q\) use, but do not reprove, the accepted graded-basis hypothesis.

## Next
The requested target is established, with the \(Q\)-rank statements conditional on that accepted basis.
